findings.statement: CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking, with up-regulation in the biopsy meta-analysis [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.81], an Open Targets genetic association among the strongest of the top genes, and several clinical-stage small-molecule antagonists (reparixin Phase 3; navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682, elubrixin, danirixin Phase 2), with Reactome neutrophil degranulation and chemokine receptor pathways. It has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument (not tested, not evidence against) and no mouse colitis phenotype in MGI, so the genetic link rests on Open Targets only.

CXCR1 shares the CXCR2 antagonists (reparixin, ladarixin, navarixin, SX-682), is up-regulated in most cohorts in the ranking and has an Open Targets genetic association, but no drug has been developed for UC specifically in these records and no MR instrument was checked.

CXCL8 is strongly and consistently up-regulated in all cohorts and has literature support, but has no Open Targets genetic association and plasma-protein MR is null [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289] and does not replicate in FinnGen: a mucosal inflammation marker without genetic support.

PD-L1 is up-regulated in all cohorts and genetically higher plasma protein lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), colocalising with an IBD GWAS signal and replicating in FinnGen. Beta is below zero, so the protective direction means PD-L1 inhibitors (approved in oncology, e.g. atezolizumab, durvalumab) would be expected to worsen, not treat, UC; the up-regulation likely reflects a counter-regulatory response. Gut eQTL not tested; no MGI colitis record.

IL12B is an established UC drug target (top Open Targets disease target) and the strongest plasma MR hit: higher protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), colocalising with IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen, so inhibition is the protective direction. Gut eQTL not tested.
IL10 plasma MR shows higher protein lowers UC risk with colocalisation, from a single instrument, consistent with a mucosal-protective role; it is also a top Open Targets UC target.

SLC26A3 is down-regulated in UC biopsies and has Open Targets genetic association; in gut cell-type eQTL MR in OLFM4+ crypt enterocyte progenitors (IBDverse), genetically predicted expression has a risk-increasing effect on UC (OR per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen. The direction is opposite to the biopsy fall, so the fall is more likely a consequence of epithelial damage than a driver; no plasma pQTL (not tested).

CXCL5 is up-regulated in all cohorts but plasma MR says higher protein lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]), replicating in FinnGen but without IBD GWAS colocalisation (tag variant, two instruments); the up-regulation is therefore not a sign that inhibition is protective.

FCGR2A has a high Open Targets genetic association and is up-regulated in all cohorts, but plasma-protein MR is null [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.68] and the gut cell eQTL is not significant; there is no drug in the records.

IDO1 is strongly up-regulated in all cohorts and has clinical-stage inhibitors (epacadostat, linrodostat), but has no Open Targets genetic association and plasma MR is not significant [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111] and colon eQTL is not significant either: an inflammation-driven marker without genetic support.

MMP1, MMP3, MMP7 and MMP10 are among the most strongly up-regulated genes in all cohorts with literature support; MMP1, MMP3 and MMP7 have broad-spectrum inhibitors (marimastat Phase 3, doxycycline Phase 4) but none has Open Targets genetic association, so they are tissue-damage biomarkers rather than genetically supported targets.

JAK2 has one of the highest Open Targets UC associations (second after IL12B) and several clinical drugs, but changes only modestly in the biopsies, so it is genetically supported without a strong expression change; JAK1 and JAK3 are the UC-relevant drugged family members.

caveats: Many genes have no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument (not tested, not evidence against).
Plasma protein is not mucosal protein; blood and gut layers were only compared where both exist (none for the leading genes).
MGI has no colitis record for CXCR2 or CD274.
Mostly one-instrument Wald ratios in gut hits; IL10 has a single instrument.
Drug lists come from Open Targets and include non-UC indications.
